newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World Red Cross body IFRC suspends Rwanda work.
newsitem.headline: World Red Cross body IFRC suspends Rwanda work.

text.p: The world Red Cross body IFRC said on Thursday it has suspended its relief work in Rwanda because of the killing of five U.N. staffers and escalating violence.
Spokesman Marie-Francoise Borel said the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies pulled 25 people out of Rwanda to Kenya and kept a skeleton staff of six.

She said resumption of work depended on security in the central African country, where gunmen killed four U.N. rights monitors -- a Briton, a Cambodian and two Rwandans -- in a Tuesday ambush in the southwest. Their wounded Rwandan driver later died.

The IFRC's work in Rwanda, where more than half a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates were slaughtered in 1994's Hutu-led genocide, includes health and housing projects and reintegration programmes for returnees.

Expatriates were the target of eight attacks in Rwanda in the last three weeks. Three Spanish aid workers were killed by unidentified gunmen and a 61-year-old Canadian missionary was shot dead by a lone gunman.
